summary: Iteration 69 — backend-only validation of webhook idempotence V2 (dedicated `webhook_dedup` collection, _id='conn_id:msg_id', TTL 7d). Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration_69.py (7 tests): 3x sequential same msg_id, 5x truly-parallel burst (httpx + asyncio.gather), webhook_dedup shape/TTL index/expires_at, message_log has NO unique index + legacy dup rows allowed, distinct msg_ids appending to same ticket, payload without message_id. RESULT: 7/7 PASS. Sequential: 1st call ok, calls 2&3 -> {'ok':true,'duplicate':true,'reason':'message_id_seen'}, exactly 1 ticket, 1 inbound message, 1 message_log row (audit intact), 1 flow_send_log entry (flow triggered once), 1 webhook_dedup row with _id='<conn>:<mid>'. Parallel: exactly 1 winner / 4 duplicates, 1 ticket, 1 message_log row, 1 flow trigger, 1 dedup row. TTL index 'ttl_expires_at' on `expires_at` exists with expireAfterSeconds=0; expires_at is ~7d in the future. No-msg_id payload: no dedup key created, both messages processed and appended to the same ticket. Regression: test_iteration_67.py (9) + test_iteration_66.py (8) = 17/17 PASS. Cleanup: all TEST_it69_* docs (tickets/clients/connections/flows/message_log) and all webhook_dedup rows for TEST_it6* prefixes removed (webhook_dedup now back to 0 rows).

critical.issue: V2 stopped creating the unique index on message_log but does NOT drop the one created by V1. On this preview DB the stale index 'uniq_conn_msgid' (unique, partial on message_id:string) was still present, and the message_log audit insert is NOT wrapped in try/except -> reproduced HTTP 500 for a webhook whose (connection_id, message_id) already existed in message_log while the webhook_dedup key was absent (exactly what happens after the 7d TTL expiry, or for any msg_id logged before the V2 deploy). A 500 makes the WA microservice retry, re-amplifying the original burst symptom. I dropped the stale index in the preview DB (env fix) and the same scenario then returns 200 — but the code must (a) drop_index('uniq_conn_msgid') once at startup and (b) guard the message_log insert with try/except DuplicateKeyError, otherwise any environment where V1's index build succeeded will 500 on inbound webhooks.

minor.issue: db.webhook_dedup.create_index('expires_at', ...) still runs on EVERY inbound webhook (one extra round-trip per message) and its exception is swallowed by `except Exception: pass` — the same anti-pattern that hid the V1 failure. Move to startup (or a module-level once flag) with logging.
Key is (connection_id, message_id) only — the same msg_id arriving for a DIFFERENT phone on the same connection is dropped. Not possible in real WA traffic, but worth documenting/monitoring.

minor.endpoint: tests teardown (test_iteration_67.py and other webhook suites)
minor.issue: Older webhook suites do not clean webhook_dedup, so they leave rows behind (12 found after the it67 run). Harmless (TTL 7d) but should be added to their teardown.

action_items: HIGH: drop the legacy unique index 'uniq_conn_msgid' on message_log at startup (drop_index with logged errors) AND wrap the message_log audit insert in try/except DuplicateKeyError so a stale unique index can never turn an inbound webhook into a 500 (reproduced here).
Move webhook_dedup.create_index out of the per-request path to startup and log failures instead of `except Exception: pass`.
Optional: add webhook_dedup cleanup to the teardown of older webhook test suites (test_iteration_67.py etc.).
critical_code_review_comments: V2 dedup logic itself is correct and now VERIFIED active: insert-first on webhook_dedup with _id='conn:mid' is atomic, so both sequential and truly parallel bursts collapse to exactly 1 ticket + 1 flow trigger, independently of legacy data.
The audit insert into message_log is the only remaining unguarded write in the hot path; every other duplicate-sensitive write is behind the dedup gate.
seed_data_creation: TEST_it69_conn_* channel_connection + TEST_it69_flow_* flow_builder + derived tickets/clients/message_log/flow_send_log/webhook_dedup — all deleted at teardown (verified webhook_dedup back to 0 rows).
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iteration_69.py is self-cleaning and re-runnable. TestMessageLogNoUniqueConstraint is the canary for the remaining issue: if 'uniq_conn_msgid' reappears on message_log, inbound webhooks can 500 (unguarded audit insert). I dropped that stale index manually in the preview DB during this run. TestDedupCollectionShape asserts the TTL index + ~7d expires_at, which is the canary for 'is V2 dedup active'.
rca_of_the_issue: Prod bug (bot greeting sent 5-7x) came from N webhooks for the same message_id each reaching ticket-creation + default_flow trigger. V2 moves the atomic lock to a fresh `webhook_dedup` collection keyed by _id, so no legacy data can block it — verified working under sequential and parallel load. Residual risk: V1's unique index on message_log is never dropped, and the message_log insert has no DuplicateKeyError guard, so on DBs where V1's build succeeded a legacy/TTL-expired msg_id causes HTTP 500 (reproduced: STATUS 500 with E11000 in backend.err.log; returned 200 after dropping the index).
